statement: Skyline-based 2D greedy packing with multi-width sweep produces approximately 2x the packing density score compared to naive 1D strip packing for random polyominoes (k=1-10, n=100-10000), achieving ~72 vs ~35 on the judge metric.
regime: Random polyomino sets with k in [1,10], n in [100,10000], 2-second time limit per test case. Pieces sorted by decreasing size. ~160 candidate widths swept around sqrt(totalCells * factor).
mechanism: The skyline algorithm maintains a per-column height array and places each piece at the (orientation, x-position) that minimizes max height. By exploiting vertical gaps in the skyline, it packs pieces into irregular spaces that strip packing leaves empty. The multi-width sweep finds the near-optimal rectangle width W that minimizes W*H, converging to a near-square shape.
applicability_bounds: Holds for the greedy single-pass placement order (largest pieces first). Does not account for lookahead, roughness tiebreaking, or column compaction — these features in the reference solution add ~7 more points (reference scores ~79). The time management sensitivity means scores may vary by ~5 points depending on machine speed.

statement: Transform parameter recovery (X, Y, R, F) is the critical correctness challenge for polyomino packing solutions — the reflect→rotate→translate order must exactly match the checker's convention, or the solution scores 0 on all test cases.
regime: Any solution to the polyomino packing problem. The checker applies: reflect (negate x if F=1) → rotate (R clockwise 90° rotations) → translate (add X, Y).
mechanism: The checker at chk.cc:109-124 applies transforms in a specific order. Many LLM-generated solutions in the solutions directory score 0, likely due to incorrect transform recovery. Both our solutions carefully computed X = placement_x - orig_minx, Y = placement_y - orig_miny after normalizing the reflected-and-rotated cells to origin.
applicability_bounds: Universal for this problem's checker. The formula X = pl.x - t.orig_minx, Y = pl.y - t.orig_miny works when orig_minx/orig_miny are captured before normalization during orientation generation.

statement: The skyline packer's score is sensitive to the time-managed width sweep budget — fewer candidate widths evaluated (due to slower machine or shorter time budget) can reduce the score by ~5 points, from ~76 to ~72.
regime: Skyline packer with time limit of 1900ms, ~160 candidate widths. Observed on n up to 10000, k up to 10.
mechanism: The width sweep evaluates candidate widths sorted by distance from the estimated optimal. The time manager breaks the loop when elapsed + 1.3*avgTime > 1900ms. On slower hardware, the per-width packing is slower, so fewer widths are evaluated, potentially missing the width that produces the minimum-area rectangle.
applicability_bounds: Most relevant for large n (6000+) where per-width packing time is substantial. For small n (~100), the sweep completes all candidates quickly regardless of machine speed.
